description: Daily diary (US participants, 30 days): six BANGS items about the participant's most recent gaming session, asked on days they had played in the previous 24 hours. 1 = strongly disagree .. 7 = strongly agree.
reference: Ballou, N., Földes, T. A., Vuorre, M., Hakman, T., Magnusson, K., & Przybylski, A. K. (2026). Open Play: A longitudinal dataset of multi-platform video game digital trace data and psychological measures (Version 2). PsyArXiv. https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/nz96c_v2
notes: Processed from the openESM harmonised copy (0075_ballou, 10.5281/zenodo.21495794); original deposit https://github.com/digital-wellbeing/open-play/tree/main/data, also CC0 1.0. Licence: CC0 1.0 with an added no-reidentification clause (LICENSE in github.com/digital-wellbeing/open-play, section 5): "Users must not attempt to reidentify, deanonymize, or otherwise link the data to specific individuals. This includes combining the dataset with other information sources for the purpose of reidentification." The clause also bars sharing derived data in a way that could enable reidentification. Cleared on #3421 (2026-11-15). Sparse per person: the median person answers each item 7 times (interquartile range 2 to 19), because most people completed only a few of the 30 daily surveys and BANGS is asked only on days they had played. These are short diaries for most people, not a dense diary. See data/ballou_2025_open_play_esm.py.
